title: Nonconvex stationarity with separate exact gradient and Hessian queries under joint smoothness
summary: The strict gradient-Hessian budget frontier is determined for derivative-only information under simultaneous gradient and Hessian Lipschitz bounds.

description_paragraphs: Find $\widehat x$ satisfying $\|\nabla f(\widehat x)\|_2\le\varepsilon$ while minimizing the gradient-query cap under a prescribed strict full-Hessian-query cap.
task.formulation: Find $\widehat x$ satisfying $\|\nabla f(\widehat x)\|_2\le\varepsilon$ while minimizing the gradient-query cap under a prescribed strict full-Hessian-query cap.

description_paragraphs: For each public finite dimension $d$, the unknown $f\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ has finite infimum, $f(x_0)-\inf f\le\Delta$, $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f)\le L_1$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla^2f)\le L_2$. All budgets and the initial point are public; derivative norms are induced Euclidean operator norms. There is no convexity or query-radius restriction.

assumptions.description: For each public finite dimension $d$, the unknown $f\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ has finite infimum, $f(x_0)-\inf f\le\Delta$, $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla f)\le L_1$ and $\operatorname{Lip}(\nabla^2f)\le L_2$. All budgets and the initial point are public; derivative norms are induced Euclidean operator norms. There is no convexity or query-radius restriction.
assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

description_paragraphs: At an arbitrary point choose exactly one of $O_g(x)=\nabla f(x)$ and $O_H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)$. A Hessian query returns the full matrix but neither the function value nor its gradient. The two counters are charged separately, and there is no function-value channel.

description_paragraphs: The error is $\|\nabla f(\widehat x)\|_2$ and the guarantee must hold deterministically on every instance.

description_paragraphs: A feasible pair $(g,h)\in\mathbb N_0^2$ is witnessed by one algorithm with $N_g\le g$ and $N_H\le h$ on every input. Define $G^\star_\infty(h;\varepsilon)$ by minimizing $g$ with a guarantee uniform over all finite dimensions. Internal subproblem solves and exact-real arithmetic are uncharged.
resource.budget: A feasible pair $(g,h)\in\mathbb N_0^2$ is witnessed by one algorithm with $N_g\le g$ and $N_H\le h$ on every input. Define $G^\star_\infty(h;\varepsilon)$ by minimizing $g$ with a guarantee uniform over all finite dimensions. Internal subproblem solves and exact-real arithmetic are uncharged.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions and outputs are arbitrary measurable functions of the observed history and public inputs. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged.
The algorithm is deterministic and uses no private random seed.
Success and both resource caps hold on every instance.
